body:
# id(world_net): create_world reads a missing or mistyped `created` flag as Ok(false) — a malformed `world_created` reply reports "exists" for a world that may not exist

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ origin/main 075b2de904)

`WorldClient::create_world` (`pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:1226`) checks only that the reply frame's `type` is `"world_created"`, then reads the outcome flag with a silent default:

- `pkgs/id/src/world_net.rs:1245` — `Ok(reply["created"].as_bool().unwrap_or(false))`

`false` is a real, meaningful answer here: the host (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs:977-986`) replies `ServerFrame::WorldCreated { world, created }` where `created: false` means the world already existed. So a `world_created` reply whose `created` field is missing or mistyped (host bug, version skew, hostile host) is indistinguishable from "already exists" — the client reports `Ok(false)` and never errors.

The sole caller trusts the bool directly:

- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:772-777` (`id world create`): `println!("{}", if result? { "created" } else { "exists" })` and exits `Ok(())` — a malformed reply prints `exists` and exits 0, telling the operator the world is there when the reply never actually said so.

Sibling `WorldClient` methods refuse exactly this shape instead of defaulting: `set_isolation` requires the field with `.context("host sent no isolation")` (`world_net.rs:1155-1158`), `info_details` requires `world_id`/`current_sequence` with context errors (`:1473-1478`), `set_schedule`/`cancel_schedule` parse via `from_value` with "host sent a malformed schedule map" (`:909`/`:943`), and `manifest_state` does the same (`:979`).

## Reproduction (probe, laptop)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-world-reply-defaults` (verbatim extraction of the reply tail `world_net.rs:1237-1245`; only the transport is replaced by passing the reply `Value` in):

- control `{"type":"world_created","world":"arena","created":true}` -> `Ok(true)`
- control `{"type":"world_created","world":"arena","created":false}` -> `Ok(false)` (legitimate "exists")
- MISSING `created` (`{"type":"world_created","world":"arena"}`) -> `Ok(false)` — silently reads as "exists"
- MISTYPED `created` (`"created":"true"`) -> `Ok(false)` — silently reads as "exists"

PROBE PASS (cargo run --offline, laptop). Note the same probe run also reproduced the `policy_request` null/verbatim behavior — that half is already tracked as #6625 and is NOT part of this issue.

## Why it matters

`id world create` is how an operator provisions a world. Today a garbled success reply produces a confident, wrong answer — "exists", exit 0 — for a world whose creation was never confirmed. The operator (or a script checking the output) proceeds as if the world is ready; the failure surfaces later, elsewhere, with no trace back to the bad reply. This is the same silent-default family as #6620 (compile) and #6621 (read_worlds), in a distinct method with a distinct user-visible lie.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorldClient::create_world` rejects a `world_created` reply whose `created` field is missing or not a bool, with an error in the existing style (e.g. "host sent no created flag" / "host sent a malformed world_created reply")
- [ ] Well-formed replies still return `Ok(true)` (newly created) and `Ok(false)` (already existed) unchanged; the refusal path (non-`world_created` type) still surfaces the host's message
- [ ] A regression test feeds `create_world` (or its reply extraction) the missing/mistyped shapes and asserts Err; the two control shapes assert Ok(true)/Ok(false)
- [ ] `cargo test -p id world_net` (laptop or CI) green, including the existing create-world-over-iroh tests (`world_session/tests.rs:1724-1770` region)

Distinct from: #6620 (compile reply defaults), #6621 (read_worlds reply drops), #6624 (caps/update_caps report), #6625 (policy_request policy) — same family, different method and consequence. The typed server side is `ServerFrame::WorldCreated { world, created }` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs:981-984`); only the client extraction is unchecked.
